findings.title: Bounds sync-back uploads positions only; reflect/soft velocity changes are lost
findings.description:
`apply_bounds_policy()` is called with both `positions` and `velocities` (lines 186-191), and the slice 140 contract describes it as mutating both in place. The sync-back mechanism is `notify_positions_modified(positions)` → `upload_positions()` only; no velocity upload exists anywhere in the driver or `GpuAgentState` interface.

For `REFLECT` (and `SOFT`, if it steers velocity), the GPU keeps the pre-bounds outward velocity. The agent is repositioned each tick, then driven back out by the next one, so it sticks to the wall instead of bouncing. The broadcast `TickResult` and the GPU state also disagree every tick.

A4 ("finite, in-bounds") would still pass, so the listed tests would not catch this. Test 7 covers wrap only.

Fix: sync back velocities as well (e.g. `notify_state_modified(positions, velocities)`), and add a reflect test asserting the velocity sign flip persists into the next tick. The claim that "same sync-back pattern" covers reflect/soft (line 209) is not true as written.

findings.title: Spawn/despawn re-upload has no defined source of truth
findings.description:
`sync_from_entity_manager()` re-uploads from `entity_manager.state`, but the design never says that state is updated on the GPU path. On the CPU path `tick(state=state, ...)` advances it in place; on the GPU path the data flow (lines 267-284) goes GPU fields → `TickResult` → broadcast, with no write-back. Three gaps follow:

- **Stale re-upload:** as written, the first spawn or despawn re-uploads positions and velocities from startup (or the last sync) and discards every GPU tick since. The design must state either that `TickResult.from_quadrants_fields` writes into `entity_manager.state` each tick, or that the sync merges current GPU state with the new/removed rows.
- **Other readers:** anything else reading `entity_manager.state` (environment `post_tick`, spawn placement, sim logger) has the same staleness question. A3 claims "zero changes" downstream without addressing it.
- **Field capacity:** `GpuAgentState` fields are allocated at `n = entity_manager.count` at setup. The design does not say what happens when count grows past that (capacity allocation, reallocation, or an explicit error), nor what happens when `setup()` runs with count 0.

Two smaller points in the same area:
- Count-equality detection misses a despawn plus spawn between two steps, which leaves the count unchanged with different agents.
- `count_changed_since_last_tick()` puts step-tracking state on `EntityManager` behind a query-named method. Letting the driver compare against the count it last uploaded is lighter and drops the `entity_manager.py` change.

findings.title: `_select_arch()` falls back by platform, not by GPU detection, so A7 is unmet
findings.description:
The plan entry and A7 (line 336) require: "a host with no Metal and no CUDA starts successfully … falls back to `qd.cpu`". The function shown returns `qd.cuda` for every Linux host and `qd.metal` for every Darwin host; the warn-and-fallback branch fires only on other OSes.

On a Linux host without CUDA (the common no-GPU case), Open Notes line 382 says `qd.init()` raises and the server exits. With `quadrants` as the default, such a host fails at startup on the default config, which directly contradicts A7.

Specify fallback on init or detection failure, not on `platform.system()`, and add the test that is currently missing: none of tests 1-8 covers A7 or asserts the WARNING is emitted.

findings.title: Internal contradictions leave implementers guessing
findings.description:
- **Bench harness:** the Files Changed table updates the import in `quadrants_fused_backend.py` (line 296). The next paragraph says the bench backends "are **not changed**" (line 301), Out of Scope excludes "any changes to the bench harness" (line 40), and A5 requires bench tests to pass "without modification". Moving `GpuAgentState` necessarily touches bench imports and probably bench tests; state that exception explicitly.
- **Walkthrough "CPU default (no GPU)":** lines 358-362 say removing the `compute:` block yields the CPU path. The default is `quadrants` (line 61, test 1), so removing the block yields the GPU path.
- **Test preamble:** "All tests are CPU-only (skip if … GPU not available)" then "tests run on Metal … on CUDA" (line 307). This leaves open whether tests 5-7 run on `qd.cpu` in GPU-less CI, which decides whether the driver has any CI coverage.
- **`arch` values:** `"cuda"` or `"metal"` at line 252, versus `"metal" | "cuda" | "cpu"` at line 224.
- **Driver interface:** it is listed twice (lines 75-94 and 217-225) and the first omits `notify_positions_modified`. Keep one.
- **Problem statement:** it says "Slices 142–149 prove" the GPU tick, a range that includes 146 itself.

findings.title: Production-to-bench dependency is only half addressed
findings.description:
Moving `GpuAgentState` to `migratory.gpu` (line 383) is the right move and correctly removes one production→bench import. But `GpuSimulationDriver.step()` also calls `build_spatial_hash` and `fused_force_integrate_kernel`, and the design does not say where those live or whether they move. I did not check the code for their location.

If they remain under `bench/backends/`, `migratory_server` still imports from the bench package, which is the dependency direction the Open Note says it eliminates. Name the modules; if they are bench-located, move them alongside `agent_state.py`.

Related: `step()` re-implements the three-phase sequence of `QuadrantsFusedTickRunner.tick_once()`. Either share one function between the two, or state why the duplication is accepted.

findings.title: Tier 2 gate conditions are under-specified
findings.description:
The Tier 2 NFR (≥60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA) is correctly restated as A6. The test does not fix the bounds policy, `subdivision_factor`, or workload density.

- The default `subdivision_factor` is 1, while line 386 names S=3 as the validated setting from slice 149.
- A non-OPEN bounds policy adds a per-tick upload on top of three downloads.

A gate run on OPEN with a sparse workload can pass while the demo configuration misses. Pin these three parameters in the test.

findings.title: Fallback performance on `qd.cpu` is unmeasured
findings.description: The plan mandates falling back to `qd.cpu`, so the design is aligned. No measurement shows the fused tick on `qd.cpu` matches the native NumPy + Numba path, which stays available as `backend: cpu`. The warning text should point users to `backend: cpu` as the likely faster option, not only as a way to suppress the warning.

findings.title: Scope, boundaries and proportionality match the slice plan entry
findings.description:
- **Scope:** the config block, driver ownership of `qd.init` and `GpuAgentState`, delegation from `SimulationManager.step()`, the unchanged `server.py` tick call site, and the stated out-of-scope items all match plan item (146).
- **Size:** one new module, one optional constructor parameter and one config dataclass are proportionate to effort 3; nothing needs cutting.
- **Contract:** the `TickResult` contract from slice 140 is preserved, using option (a) with f64 out.
- **Precision:** the f32 contract is consistent with slice 145.

findings.title: GPU init and runtime failure handling is explicit
findings.description:
- **Startup:** a `qd.init()` or allocation failure propagates and exits the server with a clear error.
- **Mid-session:** a GPU failure is declared fatal, with process restart as the recovery unit.
- **Shutdown and tests:** `finalize()` is safe after a partial setup, and the process-global `qd.init()` constraint on tests is called out.
- **Config:** invalid values fail at parse time (A1).

structured_findings.summary: Bounds sync-back uploads positions only; reflect/soft velocity changes are lost
Spawn/despawn re-upload has no defined source of truth
`_select_arch()` falls back by platform, not by GPU detection, so A7 is unmet
Production-to-bench dependency is only half addressed
Scope, boundaries and proportionality match the slice plan entry
GPU init and runtime failure handling is explicit
